text.text_excerpt: Over the years this Street, especially since Katrina of course, has really elevated itself, (oh my, no pun intended) shopping and food wise. Magazine Street follows the crescent & is easily accessible from the St Charles Trolley. You can catch it (the street) walking from Canal all the way to uptown. We spent two days there shopping, eating. (The pix of the lamps -- I bought them!) A plethora of boutiques, antiques, decorative and clothing shops plus restaurants galore. Oh, you can catch a Starbucks, but most shops are extremely unique artists' dens and galleries. Architecture in the area is interesting and much renovation is currently going on. Little bit of everything: Bars. Lots. Restaurants. Many. Shopping. Of all kinds. Services. Of all sorts . People watching. BEAUCOUP. Good drivers, who stop at pedestrian crossings. IN SHORT SUPPLY. Nevermind. LOVE Magazine Street, and it's big walk, what? 5 miles end to end? Or, Could use the # 11 bus from Canal St. Or walk over from St Charles Street car. or ride yer bicycle like I did...... Whatever u do, don't miss all the 'joys' of Magazine Street.

(Make sure to take a look at my full review which outlines everything!) I wanted to update one of my Rideshare reference points... So when you get dropped off at Scriptura and look towards Whole Foods theres a few other spots I want to highlight now that I've been here a bit longer. Past Whole Foods you'll find restaurants like Saba and Reginelli's Pizza, the Kendra Scott store, a dry cleaner, and some other more intimate spots. Up the street is Audubon park where you can then walk and eventually hit the zoo if you don't mind a stroll.
